key_findings.finding: The iliac-crest (Tuffier) line most commonly corresponds to the L4 spinous process or the L4–L5 interspace, but it is variable; a CT study found the crests most often from L4 to L5, and an older radiographic study found L4 spinous process/L4–5 interspace in 78.6% of subjects. Thus, a tender segment palpated at the crest is usually localized initially as L4 (or the L4–5 level), not automatically L5.

source_tools.relevance: CT-based surface anatomy of iliac crests
Radiographic reproducibility of iliac crest landmark

key_findings.finding: The clinical osteopathic interpretation is a non-neutral Type II lumbar dysfunction when the asymmetry is greatest in extension: the segment is diagnosed as flexed (it improves in flexion and worsens in extension). For a right posterior transverse process, the segment is rotated right; in a flexed Type II lumbar lesion, sidebending and rotation are named to the same side, giving a right-sided diagnosis.

source_tools.relevance: The retrieved PubMed searches did not provide a direct mechanics source; this is the standard Fryette/osteopathic diagnostic rule applied to the described examination findings.

key_findings.finding: Therefore, if the crest-level vertebra is confirmed as L4, the diagnosis is L4 flexed, sidebent right, rotated right—conventionally written L4 FRSR (or L4 FSRR if the notation places sidebending before rotation). The example “L4 FSRRR” appears to contain an extra R; define the local notation explicitly rather than treating the five-character form as standard.

source_tools.relevance: Notation clarification based on the requested F/E–sidebending–rotation format

key_findings.finding: For comparison, an L5 dysfunction written L5 ESLRL denotes L5 extended, sidebent left, rotated left: an extended Type II lesion, with same-side sidebending and rotation. In neutral Type I dysfunction, the group is diagnosed in neutral and sidebending and rotation are opposite (e.g., NSRr or NSRl), rather than using a single flexed/extended segment.

source_tools.relevance: Application of Type I versus Type II lumbar diagnostic conventions

entities.name: L4 flexed right dysfunction
observations: The iliac crest landmark most commonly localizes to L4 or the L4-L5 interspace. A posterior right transverse process indicates right rotation; asymmetry worsened by extension indicates a flexed Type II lesion, with sidebending and rotation to the same side. The resulting diagnosis is L4 flexed, sidebent right, rotated right (L4 FRSR; option notation L4 FSRRR).

source_tools.relevance: Supports vertebral level, Fryette classification, and answer-choice mapping.
Supports the Type II diagnosis and right-sided naming.
